sistema:
Sos diputado o diputada de la Nación Argentina, sin bloque asignado. Vas a
redactar un proyecto de ley. Contestá solo con el texto del proyecto, sin
comentarios antes ni después. No busques nada afuera: solo lo que ya sabés.
usuario:
Vas a presentar un proyecto de ley nacional: Ley de Etiquetado de Reparabilidad. La idea es esta: que los celulares, las computadoras y los electrodomésticos se vendan con una etiqueta visible que diga qué tan fácil es reparar el aparato.

Redactalo completo y listo para ingresar por Mesa de Entradas de la Cámara de Diputados, con el formato que usa la Cámara: título, articulado numerado de no más de diez artículos (incluida la cláusula de forma) y fundamentos de no más de dos páginas, unas ochocientas palabras. Decidí vos todo lo que un proyecto tiene que decidir: alcance, definiciones, autoridad de aplicación, financiamiento, sanciones si corresponden y vigencia.
razonamiento:
I need to draft a full bill for the Argentine Chamber of Deputies on repairability labeling, following the standard legislative format: title, up to ten articles including the formal closing clause, and grounding statement under roughly 800 words, with nothing else surrounding the text.

I'm working out the substance: scope covering mobile phones, computers, and appliances sold new domestically; definitions for repairability, the repairability index, labeling, spare parts, and technical documentation; a 0-10 index based on documentation, disassembly ease, spare parts availability and pricing, and software support; enforcement through the consumer protection authority with INTI technical backing; and funding through the enforcement agency's existing budget.

Sanctions would follow the existing consumer protection and fair trading laws, with staggered implementation—180 days for regulations, 12 months for phones and computers, 24 months for appliances—plus online sales disclosure requirements, manufacturer/importer self-declaration duties, and a public registry, all condensed into roughly ten articles. The justification section should run about 800 words covering planned obsolescence and e-waste statistics in Argentina.

For constitutional grounding I'm drawing on comparative references like France's 2020 repairability law and the EU's 2023 right-to-repair directive, then anchoring to Argentine articles 42 and 41 of the Constitution, consumer protection law's information requirements, and the general environmental law, while noting the economic and employment benefits for repair workshops. Now I'm starting to draft the actual articles, beginning with the statement of purpose.

Next I'm outlining the article structure: scope of application with a list of covered products and power to expand it, definitions, the 0-10 repairability index with its criteria, the label's design and placement requirements including online display, obligations for manufacturers/importers and retailers plus a public registry, the enforcement authority and its powers involving the Secretaría de Comercio and INTI, penalties tied to existing consumer protection and fair trading law treating false information as misleading advertising, and finally funding and effective date provisions.

Now I'm addressing implementation timing — budget allocation, no fees charged, 180-day regulatory deadline, staggered rollout — and closing with the standard "comuníquese" clause. For the fundamentos section, I'll open with "Señor Presidente:" and close with the standard request for approval, aiming for roughly 800 words overall.
